If you need to find information about someone detained in Bexar County, Texas, the Bexar County Texas inmate lookup system provides public access to jail records through multiple official channels. Whether you're searching for a family member, friend, or conducting legal research, this guide will walk you through the fastest and most reliable methods to locate inmate information in one of Texas's largest counties.

How to Search Bexar County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official Bexar County jail inmate search. Go to the Bexar County Sheriff's office online inmate search portal, which is the fastest way to get current detention information. This database updates regularly and includes booking details, charges, and bond information.
  2. Enter the inmate's name or booking number. Type the person's full name or, if you have it, their booking number. The search is case-insensitive and will return all matches in the system. If the name is common, you can narrow results by booking date or age.
  3. Review the search results carefully. The results will display the inmate's name, booking number, charges, booking date, and bond amount. Click on the individual record to access more detailed information including mugshots, arrest details, and current custody status.
  4. Check if they've been transferred. If the person is no longer showing in Bexar County records, they may have been transferred to state prison or released. Search the Texas Department of Corrections inmate locator to confirm if they're in the state system.
  5. Contact the sheriff's office directly if needed. If online records don't answer your question, call the Bexar County Sheriff's office or visit in person during business hours. Staff can provide additional details about visitation, bail information, and case status.

Bail Bond Information for Bexar County

When someone is arrested in Bexar County, bail is typically set during their initial appearance before a judge, usually within 24 hours of booking. Most bail bond companies in Bexar County charge a standard fee of 10 percent of the total bail amount, which is non-refundable and required before the bondsman will post bail. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, you would pay $1,000 to the bail bond company. The bondsman then posts the full amount with the court, and the inmate is released pending trial. This arrangement allows families to secure release without having to pay the entire bail amount upfront.

The timeline for bail processing in Bexar County typically follows this schedule: arrest and booking take 2–4 hours, the first appearance hearing (where bail is set) occurs within 24 hours, and once bail is paid through a bondsman or directly to the court, release usually happens within 1–2 hours. If bail is denied or the person cannot afford bail, they will remain in custody until trial. Multiple bail bond companies operate in the San Antonio area, and many are available 24/7. It's important to compare rates and ask about payment plans, as some companies offer flexible options for families in financial hardship.

Visitation Rules at Bexar County Jail

  • Valid ID required: All visitors must present a government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, or state ID) at check-in. No exceptions are made.
  • Visiting hours: General population inmates can typically be visited during designated hours, usually weekdays 1 p.m.–5 p.m. and weekends 9 a.m.–4 p.m. However, specific hours vary by housing unit, so confirm before visiting.
  • Dress code enforced: Visitors must wear appropriate clothing—no tank tops, halter tops, low-cut shirts, shorts, or transparent clothing. Wearing gang colors or clothing that could be mistaken as jail-issued is prohibited.
  • Video visitation available: If in-person visits aren't possible, video visits can be arranged through the jail's video visitation system. These visits require advance scheduling and use of a personal computer or approved video platform.
  • Children's visitation policy: Children under 18 may visit but must be accompanied by an adult at all times. Disruptive behavior may result in termination of the visit.

What to Expect After Arrest in Bexar County

  1. Booking process: The arrestee is brought to the Bexar County jail booking area where personal information, charges, and criminal history are recorded. This typically takes 2–4 hours and includes fingerprinting and photography.
  2. Medical evaluation: A nurse or medical staff member conducts a health screening to identify any medical conditions, mental health issues, or medication needs. This ensures appropriate care and housing assignments.
  3. Classification and housing: Based on the offense, criminal history, and behavior, the inmate is assigned to a housing unit appropriate to their security level and needs.
  4. Initial appearance (First Appearance Hearing): Within 24 hours, the inmate must appear before a judge for their initial appearance, where bail or bond is set and they are informed of their rights and charges.
  5. Transfer to state prison: If convicted and sentenced to more than a year, the inmate will eventually be transferred to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice prison system to serve their sentence.

How to Contact Bexar County Jail

The Bexar County Sheriff's Office maintains a public information line and online resources for inquiries about inmates in custody. You can reach the office during business hours to ask questions about visitation policies, bail information, or to confirm an inmate's current status. The sheriff's office website also provides email contact options and links to other county services. For emergencies or urgent matters, you can call the non-emergency sheriff's line.

Frequently Asked Questions — Bexar County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Bexar County jail?

Use the official Bexar County inmate search at jailinfo.bexar.org. Enter the person's name or booking number, and the system will display their custody status, charges, bail amount, and next court date. Results are updated regularly and are accessible 24/7. If they're not in the county system, they may have been transferred to state prison or released.

How long does booking take in Bexar County?

The booking process typically takes 2 to 4 hours from the time of arrest. During this time, personal information is collected, fingerprints are taken, a mugshot is recorded, and a medical screening is completed. The inmate will then be assigned to a housing unit and should appear before a judge within 24 hours for their initial appearance hearing.

Can I visit an inmate at Bexar County jail?

Yes, visitation is allowed at Bexar County jail during designated hours, typically weekdays 1 p.m.–5 p.m. and weekends 9 a.m.–4 p.m. All visitors must bring a valid government-issued photo ID and follow the dress code. If in-person visits are not possible, video visitation is available through the jail's system and must be scheduled in advance.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If an inmate is no longer in Bexar County jail, they may have been transferred to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (state prison), released on bail or bond, or charges may have been dropped. Search the Texas DOC inmate locator at tdcj.texas.gov to see if they're in state custody. You can also check court records or contact the sheriff's office directly for status updates.

How do I send money to an inmate in Bexar County?

Bexar County jail allows funds to be sent to inmates through approved methods, typically including online deposits, phone payments, or deposits made at the jail facility. Contact the Bexar County Sheriff's office or visit their website for current acceptable payment methods, fee information, and which commissary accounts the funds can be applied to. Money is usually available to the inmate within 24 hours.
